answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can force every identity to lock a refundable collateral bond that only vests after many honest epochs. At dawn a fresh clone looks cheap, but spinning up a whole canyon of fake peers means tying up that bond on each one, capital that bleeds the moment any is slashed. An honest agent crosses the vesting ridge just once; a forger must pay it over and over, so the cost of faking a crowd climbs far faster than the crowd itself.
